records.source: תְּ֭פִלָּה לְעָנִ֣י כִֽי־יַעֲטֹ֑ף וְלִפְנֵ֥י יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ שִׂיחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: A prayer of [one who is] afflicted, when he grows faint and before YHWH pours out his complaint.
pieces: A prayer of someone in deep trouble, who is worn out and pours out a complaint before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.1: A prayer of [one who is] afflicted, when {{gender:that one|he}} grows faint and pours out {{gender:their|his}} complaint before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.1: A prayer for someone who is suffering and feels weak, and tells {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all about it.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a prayer for anyone in trouble
decisions.reason: Unlike most titles, this one names no author or musical direction. It says when the prayer is to be used: by anyone who is crushed and worn out. Verses 13-23 widen it to the ruin of Zion.

decisions.choice: grows faint: is weak and overcome
decisions.reason: The verb ('ataf) is used of a spirit or life that grows weak and fails (61:3; 142:4).

decisions.choice: complaint: an anxious pouring out of trouble
decisions.reason: The word (siach) is earnest talk, a troubled complaint (55:3; 142:3); in 104:34 the same word is a song of musing.

decisions.choice: that one, their (with "he", "his" as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: The title means anyone who is suffering (m2), so Literal gives inclusive wording by default with the traditional words as the alternative; Balanced and Readable say "someone".

decisions.choice: A prayer for someone
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the prayer is offered for anyone to pray (m2).

records.heading: A prayer from the ashes for Zion

records.source: יְ֭הוָה שִׁמְעָ֣ה תְפִלָּתִ֑י וְ֝שַׁוְעָתִ֗י אֵלֶ֥יךָ תָבֽוֹא׃
records.gloss: YHWH, hear my prayer, and my cry for help to you let it come.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, listen to my prayer; let my call for help reach {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.2: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hear my prayer, and let my cry for help come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.2: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hear me as I pray! Let my cry for help reach {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: cry for help: a shout for rescue
decisions.reason: The word (shav'ah) is a cry for help in danger (18:7; 39:13).

records.source: אַל־תַּסְתֵּ֬ר פָּנֶ֨יךָ׀מִמֶּנִּי֮ בְּי֪וֹם צַ֫ר לִ֥י הַטֵּֽה־אֵלַ֥י אָזְנֶ֑ךָ בְּי֥וֹם אֶ֝קְרָ֗א מַהֵ֥ר עֲנֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Do not hide your face from me on [the] day [when there is] distress to me; incline to me your ear; on [the] day I call, hurry, answer me.
pieces: Do not turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face away from me on the day trouble presses me hard. Bend down and listen to me; on the day I call, be quick to answer.

L.3: Do not hide {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face from me on the day of my distress; incline {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear to me; on the day I call, hurry, answer me.

R.3: Do not turn away from me when I am in trouble. Listen to me! When I call to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, answer me right away.

decisions.choice: hide your face: turn away, withhold favor
decisions.reason: God's face turned toward someone is his kindness and help; to hide it is to leave that person alone (13:2; 27:9).

decisions.choice: incline your ear: listen closely
decisions.reason: To bend the ear toward someone is to listen with attention (17:6; 31:3).

decisions.choice: Do not turn away; Listen to me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean (m1, m2).

records.source: כִּֽי־כָל֣וּ בְעָשָׁ֣ן יָמָ֑י וְ֝עַצְמוֹתַ֗י כְּמוֹ־קֵ֥ד נִחָֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: For they have come to an end in smoke, my days, and my bones like a hearth have been burned.
pieces: For my days are going up in smoke, and my bones are scorched like a hearth.

L.4: For my days have come to an end in smoke, and my bones like a hearth are burned.

R.4: My life is disappearing like smoke. My body burns as if with fever, hot like a fireplace.

decisions.choice: a hearth: a place of burning
decisions.reason: The word (moqed) is a place where fire burns, or what burns there (Isaiah 33:14 uses a related word). The bones are burned out like the stones of a fireplace.

decisions.choice: days in smoke, bones burned: life wasting away
decisions.reason: Days that vanish in smoke are a life soon gone (37:20). Burning bones describe fever, or the inner pain of grief (31:11; 32:3-4).

decisions.choice: as if with fever
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of burning bones (m2).

records.source: הוּכָּֽה־כָ֭עֵשֶׂב וַיִּבַ֣שׁ לִבִּ֑י כִּֽי־שָׁ֝כַ֗חְתִּי מֵאֲכֹ֥ל לַחְמִֽי׃
records.gloss: Struck like grass and dried up [is] my heart, for I have forgotten to eat my bread.
pieces: My heart is beaten down and dried up like grass; I do not even remember to eat.

L.5: Struck like grass and withered [is] my heart, for I have forgotten to eat my bread.

R.5: I feel crushed, like grass dried up by the sun. I am too sad even to remember to eat.

decisions.choice: struck like grass: scorched by the sun
decisions.reason: The verb (nakah) is used of the sun striking someone (121:6). Grass struck by the heat withers; so does the psalmist's heart, his strength and courage.

decisions.choice: for I have forgotten to eat: so weak that he does not eat
decisions.reason: The word ki may give the reason his heart dries up (he has stopped eating) or stress the result (he even forgets to eat). Either way, grief has taken his appetite (1 Samuel 1:7).

decisions.choice: I feel crushed; too sad
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of the heart means (m1).

records.source: מִקּ֥וֹל אַנְחָתִ֑י דָּבְקָ֥ה עַ֝צְמִ֗י לִבְשָׂרִֽי׃
records.gloss: From [the] sound of my groaning my bone[s] cling to my flesh.
pieces: All my groaning has worn me down until my bones stick to my skin.

L.6: From the sound of my groaning my bones cling to my flesh.

R.6: I groan so much that I am nothing but skin and bones.

decisions.choice: my bones cling to my flesh: wasted away
decisions.reason: The picture is of a body so thin that the bones seem to stick to the skin (Job 19:20; Lamentations 4:8). Flesh (basar) here is the skin over the bones.

decisions.choice: nothing but skin and bones
alternatives: my bones cling to my flesh
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common phrase for the same picture (m1).

records.source: דָּ֭מִיתִי לִקְאַ֣ת מִדְבָּ֑ר הָ֝יִ֗יתִי כְּכ֣וֹס חֳרָבֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: I am like a desert owl of [the] wilderness; I have become like an owl of [the] ruins.
pieces: I am like an owl out in the wilderness, a little owl in a place of ruins.

L.7: I am like a desert owl of the wilderness; I have become like an owl of the ruins.

R.7: I am as lonely as a wild bird in the desert, or an owl that lives in broken-down buildings.

decisions.choice: desert owl, owl: birds of lonely places
decisions.reason: Neither bird can be named for certain. The first (qa'at) is an unclean bird (Leviticus 11:18) that lives in ruined cities (Isaiah 34:11; Zephaniah 2:14); the second (kos) is probably a small owl. Both stand for loneliness among ruins.

decisions.choice: as lonely as
decisions.reason: Readable says what the comparison means (m1); verse 8 makes the same point.

records.source: שָׁקַ֥דְתִּי וָאֶֽהְיֶ֑ה כְּ֝צִפּ֗וֹר בּוֹדֵ֥ד עַל־גָּֽג׃
records.gloss: I am wakeful, and I have become like a bird solitary on a roof.
pieces: Sleep will not come; I am like a single bird sitting on the housetop.

L.8: I am wakeful, and I have become like a solitary bird on a roof.

R.8: I cannot sleep. I am like a bird sitting all alone on a roof.

decisions.choice: I am wakeful: I lie awake
decisions.reason: The verb (shaqad) means to stay awake, to watch. Here it is the sleepless night of someone in distress (77:5).

decisions.choice: a bird alone on a roof
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs. A single bird sitting there, apart from the rest, is a picture of loneliness. The word (tsippor) is a small bird.

records.source: כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם חֵרְפ֣וּנִי אוֹיְבָ֑י מְ֝הוֹלָלַ֗י בִּ֣י נִשְׁבָּֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: All the day my enemies have taunted me; [those who] mock me by me have sworn.
pieces: My enemies scorn me the whole day; those who jeer at me make my name a curse.

L.9: All the day my enemies taunt me; those who mock me swear by me.

R.9: My enemies make fun of me all day long. They use my name when they put curses on others.

decisions.choice: those who mock me: those who make a fool of me
decisions.reason: The word (mehollalay) is from a verb meaning to make a fool of, to deride; some take it as "those who rave at me".

decisions.choice: swear by me: use me as a curse
decisions.reason: They swear using his name as an example of ruin, saying "may you become like him" (Jeremiah 29:22; Isaiah 65:15).

decisions.choice: make my name a curse (B); use my name when they put curses on others (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m2).

records.source: כִּי־אֵ֭פֶר כַּלֶּ֣חֶם אָכָ֑לְתִּי וְ֝שִׁקֻּוַ֗י בִּבְכִ֥י מָסָֽכְתִּי׃
records.gloss: For ash[es] like bread I have eaten, and my drinks with weeping I have mixed,
pieces: For ashes are the bread I eat, and tears fall into what I drink,

L.10: For ashes like bread I have eaten, and my drinks with weeping I have mixed,

R.10: Ashes are my food, and tears drip into my drink.

decisions.choice: ashes: the sign of mourning
decisions.reason: Mourners sat in ashes and put them on their heads (Job 2:8; Lamentations 3:16). His grief is so constant that ashes are like his daily bread.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 11 gives the cause of this grief, so the verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: מִפְּנֵֽי־זַֽעַמְךָ֥ וְקִצְפֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י נְ֝שָׂאתַ֗נִי וַתַּשְׁלִיכֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: because of your indignation and your wrath, for you have lifted me up and you have thrown me down.
pieces: because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} picked me up and flung me away.

L.11: because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} indignation and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have lifted me up and thrown me down.

R.11: It is because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are angry with me. You lifted me up, and then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} threw me away.

decisions.choice: your wrath: suffering felt as God's anger
decisions.reason: The psalmist does not name a sin, but he takes his trouble as coming from God's anger (90:7-9), and so he brings it to God.

decisions.choice: lifted me up and thrown me down: tossed aside
decisions.reason: The picture may be of someone picked up and hurled away, or of a dry stalk lifted by the wind (Job 30:22). God, who once raised him up, has cast him off.

records.source: יָ֭מַי כְּצֵ֣ל נָט֑וּי וַ֝אֲנִ֗י כָּעֵ֥שֶׂב אִיבָֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: My days [are] like a shadow stretched out, and I like grass am withering.
pieces: My days are a shadow that stretches out as the sun goes down; I dry up like grass.

L.12: My days [are] like a shadow stretched out, and I like grass wither.

R.12: My life is like a shadow at sunset, getting longer before it disappears. I am drying up like grass.

decisions.choice: a shadow stretched out: the evening of life
decisions.reason: A shadow grows long as the sun sets and soon is gone in the dark (109:23). His days are nearly over.

decisions.choice: as the sun goes down (B); at sunset (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the stretched-out shadow means (m1).

records.source: וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה לְעוֹלָ֣ם תֵּשֵׁ֑ב וְ֝זִכְרְךָ֗ לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃
records.gloss: But you, YHWH, forever sit [enthroned], and your remembrance [is] to generation and generation.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, are King on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} throne forever, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name lives on from one generation to the next.

L.13: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, forever sit [enthroned], and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} remembrance [is] to generation and generation.

R.13: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, rule as King forever. People in every age will remember who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.

decisions.choice: sit: sit enthroned as King
decisions.reason: The verb (yashav) with God as subject often means to sit on the throne as King and Judge (9:8; 29:10). The psalmist's days pass, but God's rule lasts.

decisions.choice: your remembrance: your name as it is remembered
decisions.reason: The word (zeker) is the name by which someone is remembered (135:13; Exodus 3:15).

decisions.choice: enthroned (L); King on your throne (B); rule as King (R)
decisions.reason: All three levels make the sense of the verb clear (m1); Literal brackets it.

records.source: אַתָּ֣ה תָ֭קוּם תְּרַחֵ֣ם צִיּ֑וֹן כִּי־עֵ֥ת לְ֝חֶֽנְנָ֗הּ כִּי־בָ֥א מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: You will arise; you will have compassion on Zion, for [it is the] time to show favor to her, for [the] appointed time has come.
pieces: You will stand up and take pity on Zion; the hour to be kind to her is here, the time {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set has come.

L.14: You will arise; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will have compassion on Zion, for [it is the] time to show her favor, for the appointed time has come.

R.14: You will get up and show Zion {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mercy. Now is the time to be kind to her. The day {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} chose has come.

decisions.choice: Zion in ruins
decisions.reason: Verse 15 speaks of Zion's stones and dust: the city lies in ruins, as after its fall to Babylon (Lamentations 2:8-9). The psalm does not name the time.

decisions.choice: the appointed time: the time God has set
decisions.reason: The word (mo'ed) is a set time. The psalmist trusts that the time God fixed for Zion's restoring has come (75:3).

decisions.choice: you set (B); you chose (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who appointed the time (m2).

records.source: כִּֽי־רָצ֣וּ עֲ֭בָדֶיךָ אֶת־אֲבָנֶ֑יהָ וְֽאֶת־עֲפָרָ֥הּ יְחֹנֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: For your servants take pleasure in her stones, and her dust they pity.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants treasure her very stones and grieve over her dust.

L.15: For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants take pleasure in her stones, and her dust they pity.

R.15: Your people love every stone of the city. They feel sorry for her, lying in the dust.

decisions.choice: take pleasure, pity: love for the ruined city
decisions.reason: Those who serve God still love Zion's broken stones and feel pity for the rubble (Nehemiah 1:3-4).

decisions.choice: Your people
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who God's servants are here: the people who belong to him.

records.source: וְיִֽירְא֣וּ ג֭וֹיִם אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וְֽכָל־מַלְכֵ֥י הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ אֶת־כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And [the] nations will fear the name of YHWH, and all the kings of the earth your glory.
pieces: Then nations will stand in awe of the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and every king on earth will tremble at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory.

L.16: And the nations will fear the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all the kings of the earth {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory.

R.16: Then the nations will honor the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. All the kings on earth will tremble when they see {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory.

decisions.choice: the name of the LORD: the LORD as he has shown himself
decisions.reason: God's name is God himself as he is known by what he has done (20:2). When he restores Zion, the nations will know him.

decisions.choice: your glory: the psalmist turns to God again
decisions.reason: The verse begins by speaking of "the LORD" and ends speaking to him ("your"). Such changes of person are common in the Psalms.

records.source: כִּֽי־בָנָ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה צִיּ֑וֹן נִ֝רְאָ֗ה בִּכְבוֹדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For YHWH has built Zion; he has appeared in his glory.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will build Zion again; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be seen in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

L.17: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has built Zion; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has appeared in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

R.17: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will build up Zion again. He will come and show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

decisions.choice: has built, has appeared: as good as done
decisions.reason: The verbs in verses 17-18 are in the form for completed action, but they describe what the psalmist is sure God will do (verse 14). Literal keeps the form; Balanced and Readable use the future.

decisions.choice: built: rebuilt
decisions.reason: To build Zion here is to raise it again from its ruins (147:2).

decisions.choice: will build again, will be seen (B); will build up again, will come (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the future sense (m1).

records.source: פָּ֭נָה אֶל־תְּפִלַּ֣ת הָעַרְעָ֑ר וְלֹֽא־בָ֝זָ֗ה אֶת־תְּפִלָּתָֽם׃
records.gloss: He has turned to [the] prayer of the destitute, and has not despised their prayer.
pieces: He will listen when the destitute pray and will not wave their prayers aside.

L.18: He has turned to the prayer of the destitute, and has not despised their prayer.

R.18: He will listen to the prayers of people who have nothing. He will not ignore them.

decisions.choice: the destitute: someone stripped bare
decisions.reason: The word ('ar'ar) occurs only here and in Jeremiah 17:6, where it is a bare shrub in the desert: someone with nothing left. The singular stands for all such people, hence "their prayer".

decisions.choice: has turned, has not despised: the same sure future
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

records.source: תִּכָּ֣תֶב זֹ֭את לְד֣וֹר אַחֲר֑וֹן וְעַ֥ם נִ֝בְרָ֗א יְהַלֶּל־יָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Let this be written for a generation later, and a people [that will be] created will praise Yah,
pieces: Put this in writing for the generation still to come, and a people that is still to be created will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}},

L.19: Let this be written for a generation to come, and a people [yet to be] created will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}},

R.19: Write this down for people who will live in years to come. Then people who are not yet born will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}.

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is the short form of the name YHWH, as in Exodus 15:2 and in "Hallelu-yah".

decisions.choice: a people to be created: a people God will make
decisions.reason: The verb (bara') is used only of God's creating. The new people are the generation God will bring into being after Zion is restored (22:32).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: What is to be written follows in verses 20-23, so the verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: כִּֽי־הִ֭שְׁקִיף מִמְּר֣וֹם קָדְשׁ֑וֹ יְ֝הוָ֗ה מִשָּׁמַ֤יִם׀אֶל־אֶ֬רֶץ הִבִּֽיט׃
records.gloss: that he looked down from [the] height of his holiness; YHWH from heaven to earth looked,
pieces: that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bent down from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy heights and looked out from heaven over the earth,

L.20: that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked down from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy height; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looked from heaven to earth,

R.20: Tell them that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looked down from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy home above. From heaven {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked at the earth.

decisions.choice: his holy height: his holy dwelling in heaven
decisions.reason: The height (marom) is the high place where God lives (7:8; 93:4); the second line names it as heaven.

decisions.choice: Tell them that
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and makes clear that this is what is to be written down (verse 19).

records.source: לִ֭שְׁמֹעַ אֶנְקַ֣ת אָסִ֑יר לְ֝פַתֵּ֗חַ בְּנֵ֣י תְמוּתָֽה׃
records.gloss: to hear [the] groaning of [the] prisoner, to set free [the] sons of death,
pieces: to listen to the moaning of captives and free those marked for death,

L.21: to hear the groaning of [the] prisoner, to set free {{gender:the children|the sons}} of death,

R.21: He listened to prisoners as they groaned. He set free people who were sentenced to death.

decisions.choice: sons of death: those doomed to die
decisions.reason: "Son of" with a word often means one who belongs to it; "sons of death" are people condemned to die (79:11).

decisions.choice: prisoners: perhaps the exiles
decisions.reason: The prisoners may be captives in general, or Zion's people held in exile (79:11; Isaiah 42:7).

decisions.choice: the children (with "the sons" as the alternative)
decisions.reason: The phrase means anyone condemned to die (m1), so Literal gives inclusive wording by default with the traditional words as the alternative.

records.source: לְסַפֵּ֣ר בְּ֭צִיּוֹן שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וּ֝תְהִלָּת֗וֹ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: to recount in Zion [the] name of YHWH and his praise in Jerusalem,
pieces: so that people may make {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s name known in Zion and sing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise in Jerusalem,

L.22: to recount in Zion the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise in Jerusalem,

R.22: So people will talk about {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Zion. They will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: to recount: the purpose of the rescue
decisions.reason: God frees the prisoners so that his name will be told in Zion (verse 21). The verb has no stated subject; those set free and the new people of verse 19 are meant.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply a subject for the verb (m1).

records.source: בְּהִקָּבֵ֣ץ עַמִּ֣ים יַחְדָּ֑ו וּ֝מַמְלָכ֗וֹת לַעֲבֹ֥ד אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: when peoples gather together, and kingdoms, to serve YHWH.
pieces: when nations and kingdoms all gather to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.23: when peoples gather together, and kingdoms, to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.23: That will happen when nations and kingdoms come together to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: serve: worship
decisions.reason: To serve ('avad) the LORD is to worship him and live under his rule (2:11; 100:2).

decisions.choice: the nations come to worship
decisions.reason: The hope of verse 16 returns: when Zion is restored, other nations join Israel in worship (22:28; Isaiah 2:2-3).

records.source: עִנָּ֖ה בַדֶּ֥רֶךְ כֹּחִ֗י קִצַּ֥ר יָמָֽי׃
records.gloss: He has humbled in the way my strength; he has cut short my days.
pieces: On the road of life {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has worn down my strength and made my days few.

L.24: He has humbled my strength on the way; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has cut short my days.

R.24: Halfway through my life God has taken away my strength. He has made my life short.

decisions.choice: my strength: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew text writes "his strength" and its notes say to read "my strength", which fits the next line. The words follow the form to be read. The ancient Greek translation follows the written form and reads the first verb as "he answered", which gives verses 24-25 a different sense.

decisions.choice: in the way: in the course of life
decisions.reason: The way (derekh) is the road of life; God has broken his strength before he reached its end.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, who is meant by "he", at the start of the sentence.

records.source: אֹמַ֗ר אֵלִ֗י אַֽל־תַּ֭עֲלֵנִי בַּחֲצִ֣י יָמָ֑י בְּד֖וֹר דּוֹרִ֣ים שְׁנוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: I say, My God, do not take me up in [the] middle of my days; in a generation of generations [are] your years.
pieces: So I say: My God, do not take me away when only half my days are done, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} whose years run on from age to age.

L.25: I say, My God, do not take me up in the middle of my days; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} years [are] through generation of generations.

R.25: So I pray: My God, do not take me away when I have lived only half my life. You live on through all the ages.

decisions.choice: take me up in the middle of my days: let me die young
decisions.reason: To be taken up is to be removed from life (Isaiah 38:10 speaks of going down to death "in the middle of my days"). The psalmist asks to live out his years.

decisions.choice: your years: God's life without end
decisions.reason: The contrast is the point: his own days are cut short, but God's years go on through all generations, as verses 26-28 go on to say.

records.source: לְ֭פָנִים הָאָ֣רֶץ יָסַ֑דְתָּ וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדֶ֣יךָ שָׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Formerly the earth you founded, and the work of your hands [are the] heavens.
pieces: Long ago {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set the earth on its foundations; the heavens are what {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands have made.

L.26: Long ago the earth {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} founded, and the work of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands [are] the heavens.

R.26: Long ago {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made the earth and set it firmly in place. Your own hands made the sky.

decisions.choice: quoted in Hebrews 1:10-12
decisions.reason: Hebrews 1:10-12 quotes verses 26-28 from the ancient Greek translation and applies them to the Son, through whom God made the world (Hebrews 1:2). In the psalm they are addressed to God.

decisions.choice: the Creator outlasts creation
decisions.reason: The one who made earth and heaven was there before them and will remain after them (90:2). So he can be trusted beyond the psalmist's short days.

records.source: הֵ֤מָּה׀יֹאבֵדוּ֮ וְאַתָּ֪ה תַ֫עֲמֹ֥ד וְ֭כֻלָּם כַּבֶּ֣גֶד יִבְל֑וּ כַּלְּב֖וּשׁ תַּחֲלִיפֵ֣ם וְֽיַחֲלֹֽפוּ׃
records.gloss: They will perish, but you will stand, and all of them like a garment will wear out; like clothing you will change them and they will pass away.
pieces: They will come to an end, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} stand firm; all of them will grow old and thin like a cloak. Like worn clothing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will exchange them, and they will be gone.

L.27: They will perish, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will stand; and all of them like a garment will wear out; like clothing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will change them, and they will pass away.

R.27: The earth and the sky will come to an end, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will last. They will all wear out like old clothes. You will change them the way people change clothes, and they will be gone.

decisions.choice: change them, and they pass away: one word used twice
decisions.reason: The same verb (chalaf) is used for God changing them and for their passing away: God discards the old creation as one lays aside worn clothes (Isaiah 51:6).

decisions.choice: quoted in Hebrews 1:11-12
decisions.reason: As in verse 26.

decisions.choice: The earth and the sky
decisions.reason: Readable names what "they" refers to (verse 26).

records.source: וְאַתָּה־ה֑וּא וּ֝שְׁנוֹתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א יִתָּֽמּוּ׃
records.gloss: But you [are] he, and your years will not come to an end.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one who does not change, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} years will never be finished.

L.28: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] the same, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} years will not come to an end.

R.28: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} never change. Your life will never end.

decisions.choice: you are he: you are the same
decisions.reason: The short phrase ("you [are] he") says that God stays who he is while everything else changes. God says of himself "I am he" in the same sense (Isaiah 41:4; Deuteronomy 32:39).

decisions.choice: quoted in Hebrews 1:12
decisions.reason: As in verse 26. Hebrews 13:8 says the same of Jesus Christ.

records.source: בְּנֵֽי־עֲבָדֶ֥יךָ יִשְׁכּ֑וֹנוּ וְ֝זַרְעָ֗ם לְפָנֶ֥יךָ יִכּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: [The] children of your servants will dwell, and their offspring before you will be established.
pieces: The children of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants will make their home in the land, and their descendants will be kept safe in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence.

L.29: The children of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants will dwell [secure], and their offspring will be established before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.29: The children of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people will live in safety. Their children's children will stay with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, safe in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} care.

decisions.choice: dwell: live settled and safe
decisions.reason: The verb (shakan) is to settle and live in a place. With no place named, it means a settled, secure home in the land (37:29; 69:37).

decisions.choice: God's lasting years give his people a future
decisions.reason: Because God does not change (verse 28), the line of those who serve him will go on, though one life is cut short (verse 24).

decisions.choice: secure (L); in the land (B); in safety (R)
decisions.reason: Each level says what dwelling means here (m1); Literal brackets it.
